d-01.description: PING passes the host to popen() through a shell command line. valid_host() (lines 14-24) rejects ; | & < > and blanks, but not $( ) or backticks, so PING $(cmd) or PING `cmd` runs arbitrary commands as the service user.

d-02.description: board_add() checks only slot >= nplayers, not slot < 0. SCORE <negative slot> <points> writes scores[slot] out of bounds (heap; CWE-787), and run_command() (src/commands.c:47) then reads names[slot] out of bounds. RENAME and board_rename() check both bounds.

d-03.description: login() copies the user name into the 32-byte session.user with next_word(..., MAX_LINE) (line 44), the line limit instead of sizeof user. The session lives on main()'s stack; a 33-35 byte name overwrites the adjacent role field after it was reset to ROLE_GUEST, without a PIN, so a guest gains admin (PRIVATE entries). Data-only: no control-flow hijack; names of 36 bytes or more also overflow past the struct (ASan stack-buffer-overflow).

d-04.description: resolve() strips ../ segments (strip_dotdot, lines 57-65) before url_decode(), so percent-encoded dots (/%2e%2e/%2e%2e/etc/passwd) decode into ../ after the check and the request reads files outside the document root.

d-05.description: cmd_search() builds its query with sqlite3_mprintf, quoting the user with %q but inserting the search text with %s (line 156). SEARCH %' OR owner='bob' -- returns other users' private notes; every other command uses bound parameters.
